payload.message: • Requirements fixed: 300 passengers; 6000 km range; take-off ≤ 85 m/s; landing ≤ 72 m/s. • Unstated values are assumed and marked. • Weight rides on the passenger count; the whole answer rides on weight.
• Hypothesis: L/D climbs with aspect ratio, so push span to the limit. • Low-speed limits floor the area; Breguet ties range to L/D. • Expect the optimum where landing speed caps aspect ratio.

payload.title: Aircraft L/D optimization: 300 pax, 6000 km
abstract: We searched a 96-wing design space for the highest cruise L/D meeting the stated mission requirements.
The best feasible wing reaches L/D 19.7 ± 1.9 (95%) at span 64 m and aspect ratio 13.7; 30 designs were infeasible on low-speed or range.
The winner stands on a solved wing polar with a stated non-wing buildup.
methods: Weights from the passenger count via a payload fraction; MTOW carries a mild span-structural penalty.
Screening L/D from a drag polar (induced drag over aspect ratio and Oswald efficiency, parasite drag with sweep).
Feasibility from stall-speed limits for take-off and landing and a Breguet range check.

The top 9 feasible finalists were built as parametric geometry and solved by a vortex-lattice method in parallel; the cruise point was interpolated on each solved polar, and the winner was picked on solved numbers.

results.reason: wing solved by vortex lattice; non-wing parasite drag from a stated component buildup

uncertainty: The trade, L/D rising with aspect ratio until the landing speed caps it, is physical and trustworthy.
Wing induced and viscous drag are solved; the non-wing parasite share is a stated buildup.
The optimum sits between discrete grid points, so the reported design is the best sampled, not the continuous optimum.
next_investigations: Cruise Mach trade: sweep cruise Mach against the fixed requirements to find where the range-speed-L/D surface actually peaks
Composite-span structural limits: explore spans beyond today's structural cap with a composite wing-box weight model driving MTOW
Full-configuration solve: put the fuselage and tail in the solved model and trim the winner for static margin
